name: Thelsamar Blood Sausages
summary: At Thelsamar's Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove keeps Thelsamar Blood Sausages on the table. A favorite across Loch Modan, they need fresh ingredients from the valley.

sections.title: A Hearty Highland Dish
sections.body: Hungry children and miners returning from the Ironband Excavation fill Thelsamar's tavern. Vidra Hearthstove tends the stove, making sausages known across Loch Modan. Her recipe draws on wildlife from the rugged mountain pass.

sections.title: Unconventional Spices
sections.body: Vidra uses boar intestines for casings and bear meat for the filling. Spider ichor gives the sausages their sharp, pungent bite. Gathering the entrails and venomous fluid takes a steady stomach, though travelers come to appreciate this regional favorite.

faq.answer: Vidra Hearthstove cooks at the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. She takes pride in feeding Loch Modan's hard-working folk, especially laborers from nearby excavation sites.

faq.q: Why does the recipe use spider ichor?
faq.answer: Vidra adds spider ichor to give her blood sausages a sharp, pungent flavor.
Thelsamar's townspeople, children, and weary workers returning from shifts at the Ironband Excavation eat the sausages.
Black bears, mountain boars, and wood lurker spiders roam Loch Modan's wilderness and wooded hills around the lake.

faq.q: What casing is used for the sausages?
faq.answer: Vidra uses casings cleaned from local mountain boars to hold bear meat and seasoned filling together over the fire.

faq.q: Do travelers learn to cook these sausages?
faq.answer: Yes. Bring Vidra the ingredients, and she shares the recipe with travelers who know how to cook.

angles.text: Gather ingredients for Vidra, and aspiring cooks can learn the Blood Sausage recipe for hearty field rations.
As a dwarf, blood sausage is familiar comfort food, shaped by the rugged tastes of Khaz Modan's mountain clans.
As an Alliance member, you can help feed Thelsamar's workforce as they maintain key infrastructure and excavate ancient ruins across Loch Modan.
